skill.name: alembic
skill.description: Guidance for creating, applying, and managing Alembic database migrations in SQLAlchemy projects.
skill.summary: Manage SQLAlchemy database schema changes with Alembic commands, configuration examples, and migration patterns.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences containing Alembic commands, Python migration snippets, and normal database configuration examples. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable marketplace behavior was found in the reviewed skill content.

remediation.issue: Command examples can affect real databases if copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning to run migration commands only against the intended environment and to back up production data before downgrades.

remediation.issue: Database URL examples may encourage passing credentials directly in code.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend loading connection strings from a local secret manager or environment configuration and avoiding committed credentials.

content.value_statement: Database schema changes are risky when teams lack repeatable migration patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Alembic guidance for SQLAlchemy projects.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to create, apply, downgrade, and inspect Alembic migrations.
Provides async SQLAlchemy env.py configuration patterns.
Explains manual schema operations such as columns, indexes, constraints, and table renames.
Covers SQLite batch mode, object filtering, and migration branch handling.
Includes examples for data migrations and programmatic migration checks.
limitations: Does not execute migrations or inspect a database by itself.
Requires an existing Python project with SQLAlchemy models and Alembic installed.
Examples must be adapted to each project database and deployment workflow.
Does not replace database backups or production migration review.

use_cases.title: Create model-driven migrations
use_cases.description: Generate Alembic revisions from SQLAlchemy model changes and review the resulting schema operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare safe database releases
use_cases.description: Plan upgrade, downgrade, and status commands before applying schema changes across environments.

use_cases.title: Maintain migration configuration
use_cases.description: Configure async engines, metadata discovery, object filters, and SQLite batch mode for reliable autogeneration.

prompt_templates.title: Create my first migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new SQLAlchemy schema change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an Alembic migration for my SQLAlchemy model changes. Show the commands to generate, inspect, and apply it safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review an autogenerated migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a generated migration before running it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Alembic migration plan for safety. Identify risky operations, missing downgrade steps, and changes that need manual edits.

prompt_templates.title: Configure async Alembic
prompt_templates.scenario: Set up env.py for async SQLAlchemy projects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through configuring Alembic env.py for async SQLAlchemy. Include metadata setup, async engine configuration, and autogenerate options.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production migration strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a real database release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a safe Alembic migration strategy for a production schema change with data backfill, rollback planning, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: I added an email column to the users model. What should I do next?
output_examples.output: The skill would outline an autogenerate command, review steps for the generated migration, an upgrade command, and checks for downgrade behavior.

output_examples.input: My SQLite migration cannot alter a table directly.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend Alembic batch mode and explain when render_as_batch should be enabled for SQLite migrations.

output_examples.input: I need to check if the database is at the latest revision.
output_examples.output: The skill would describe comparing current database heads with Alembic script heads and when to use that check in deployment workflows.

best_practices: Review autogenerated migrations before applying them to shared or production databases.
Test both upgrade and downgrade paths in a disposable database before release.
Keep schema migrations and data migrations small enough to review and roll back.
anti_patterns: Do not downgrade or reset a production database without backups and an approved rollback plan.
Do not commit database credentials in alembic.ini or migration files.
Do not trust autogenerate output without checking constraints, indexes, data changes, and defaults.

faq.question: Does this skill run Alembic commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You decide which commands to run in your project.

faq.question: Can it help with async SQLAlchemy projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes env.py patterns for async engines and SQLAlchemy metadata configuration.

faq.question: Does it support SQLite migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Alembic batch mode, which is often required for SQLite table changes.

faq.question: Can it create data migrations?
faq.answer: It shows patterns for combining schema changes with SQL updates, but you must adapt them to your data model.

faq.question: Is it safe for production databases?
faq.answer: It can help plan production migrations, but you still need backups, review, testing, and deployment controls.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
